name: Modafinil

card.summary: Prescription wakefulness drug that forums treat as a study and productivity aid; no appearance effect has been studied.
card.note: Prescription-only in the US; label warns of serious rash and psychiatric symptoms.

quick.overview:
Modafinil is an FDA-approved prescription drug for excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work disorder. In looksmaxxing and self-improvement forums it is discussed as a way to stay alert and productive.

No trial has tested it for appearance. Posters link it to looks only indirectly, such as appetite suppression or feeling more sociable.
quick.mechanism: The label says its mechanism is unknown. A 2009 imaging study in healthy men found it binds the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine.
quick.risks: The label warns of serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, hypersensitivity reactions, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events. Users report headache and reduced appetite. It is prescription-only in the US.

chain: More study, work and training time and less fatigue
Indirect gains in routine, energy and presentation; appetite suppression noted by some users
angle.text: People use modafinil to stay alert and focused, which they link to more productive days and sometimes to more energy for gym and grooming routines. Forum users also report reduced appetite, which some connect to leaner bodies; no direct cosmetic mechanism has been described.

lead: Modafinil is a prescription wakefulness-promoting medication, often grouped as a eugeroic, that the US Food and Drug Administration has approved to improve wakefulness in adults with excessive sleepiness from narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea or shift work disorder [4]. It was developed in France by Laboratoire Lafon and is the main active metabolite of an earlier compound, adrafinil [1][15].

People in looksmaxxing and wider self-improvement communities use it as a way to stay alert, study, work and train through long days. The chain they describe runs from more alert hours, to more productive work and gym sessions, to steadier routines and a more energetic, sociable presentation; some also note appetite suppression, which a few connect to leaner physiques [8][9][28]. Posters use phrases such as "lifemaxxing" and one thread title calls it an "ultimate looks and lifemaxxing drug" [28]. No published trial has tested modafinil for a facial or body appearance outcome.

Its mechanism is not fully known; the label says so, while imaging work in healthy men found that it occupies the dopamine transporter and raises dopamine [3][4]. Reviews of its effect on cognition in healthy, rested adults report small or mixed effects, a debate summarized below [20][21]. The label carries warnings that include serious rash, hypersensitivity reactions and psychiatric symptoms [4]. It is a Schedule IV prescription drug in the US and is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's in-competition list [15].
infobox: Label reports growth restriction and miscarriage; controlled studies lacking [4]

paras: The US label lists three indications: excessive sleepiness associated with narcolepsy, obstructive sleep apnea and shift work disorder. For sleep apnea the label specifies that the drug treats sleepiness, not the underlying airway obstruction, and that maximal effort to use continuous positive airway pressure should come first where it is the treatment of choice [4].

Off-label interest has included depression, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder and schizophrenia. A 2008 review described initial promise in these areas while noting that the evidence was early [2]. A 2022 network meta-analysis of augmentation agents in treatment-resistant depression, covering 65 studies, listed modafinil among the agents with a significant response-rate advantage over placebo [27]. A 2018 network meta-analysis of ADHD drugs included modafinil among the medicines compared [5]. Registered trials have also looked at fatigue in multiple sclerosis and cancer, and at post-traumatic stress disorder [12][29].

Students, shift workers, professionals and others use modafinil without a medical indication to stay alert or study for long stretches. Wikipedia notes use by self-described transhumanists and office workers, and by the French, US and UK militaries as an alternative to amphetamines for fatigue [15]. The Nootropic article reports that the American Medical Association adopted a policy in 2016 discouraging prescription of cognitive enhancers to healthy people, citing variable, dose-dependent and modest effects [19].
A registered phase 4 trial examined attention, memory and executive function in 128 university students [6].

On looksmax.org, modafinil is discussed alongside Adderall as a study and work aid [8][9]. A medical student described studying a full subject over 14 hours without brain fog or caffeine jitters, while also reporting headache, no appetite and joint aches [8]. Another poster said it made him "more awake and charismatic" and more productive [18]. Others note that reduced appetite complicates a lean bulk [8].

T Nation forum users, whose threads centre on lifting and physique, discuss it as a brain-function booster. One poster said a modafinil prescription taken off-label for attention problems had been tied to nausea before workouts [30], and another said a relative with narcolepsy found it very helpful [31]. A looksmax.org thread title also frames it as a general 'lifemaxxing' tool, in keeping with the idea that alertness and energy support the gym, grooming and social routines that shape appearance [28].

The label states that the mechanism is unknown, and that modafinil-induced wakefulness can be attenuated by an alpha-1 adrenergic antagonist [4]. A 2009 JAMA imaging study in healthy men reported that modafinil binds the dopamine transporter and increases dopamine in the brain, including the nucleus accumbens [3]. A 2001 paper examined the dopaminergic role in stimulant-induced wakefulness [10]. Research on the orexin system, whose loss produces a narcolepsy-like phenotype in mice, forms part of the background to wake-promoting drug research [11].

A 2005 randomized trial reported that modafinil produced sympathomedullary activation, with effects on blood pressure and catecholamine measures [24]. Wikipedia describes modafinil as acting mainly as a weak, atypical dopamine reuptake inhibitor with little affinity for serotonin or norepinephrine transporters [15].

Wikipedia gives oral bioavailability of roughly 40 to 65 percent, peak levels 2 to 4 hours after a dose, about 60 percent protein binding and an elimination half-life of 12 to 15 hours (armodafinil 10 to 17 hours). It is a weak to moderate inducer of the liver enzyme CYP3A4, which can lower the levels of some other drugs, including hormonal contraceptives [15].

Armodafinil is the longer-acting R-enantiomer, introduced in 2007 [15]. Adrafinil is the parent compound that the body converts to modafinil; a T Nation poster compared the two [32][15]. Pitolisant, which acts on histamine receptors, was compared against placebo and modafinil in a European double-blind trial in narcolepsy [26]. A 2024 randomized non-inferiority trial compared modafinil with amphetamine-dextroamphetamine in idiopathic hypersomnia and narcolepsy type 2 [25].

Most modafinil trials have enrolled patients with sleep disorders, and the US label's indications rest on them [4]. Wikipedia summarises that in a 12-week shift-work trial modafinil improved nighttime wakefulness and reduced commute accidents although sleepiness often persisted, that for sleep apnea it moderately reduces daytime sleepiness, and that meta-analyses in multiple sclerosis fatigue show modest effects [15]. A phase 3 adult ADHD programme reported it did not meet its aim, with high rates of side effects and discontinuation [15]. A pediatric phase 3 trial studied sleepiness in children and adolescents with narcolepsy [7].

In healthy people the literature is more mixed. The 2008 Neuropsychopharmacology review discussed the open question of whether any cognitive benefit exceeds simple wakefulness [2]. A 2015 systematic review by Battleday and Brem of studies from 1990 to 2014 in healthy, non-sleep-deprived adults found that simple tests mostly showed better executive function, about half showed gains in attention, learning or memory, and complex tasks more consistently showed improvements; it found no consistent pattern of side effects or mood change [20]. A 2020 set of meta-analyses of 47 studies reported a small overall improvement from modafinil, with a specific benefit for memory updating, and concluded that the belief that these drugs are effective enhancers was not supported by current evidence [21]. A pilot randomized study of caffeine, methylphenidate and modafinil in healthy men found moderate effects for caffeine and methylphenidate and no significant effect of modafinil on its test battery [22]. A companion analysis of memory and brain connectivity in healthy adults was also published [23]. Wikipedia reports that effects in healthy people range from significant gains to little or none, and are more noticeable in sleep-deprived people [15].

Registered trials have examined multiple sclerosis fatigue, cancer-related fatigue, post-traumatic stress disorder, remitted depression with cognitive impairment and stimulant dependence, with statuses ranging from completed to terminated [12][13][14][29]. No studies were found testing modafinil for facial or body appearance outcomes.

The label lists serious rash including Stevens-Johnson syndrome, angioedema and anaphylaxis, multi-organ hypersensitivity, persistent sleepiness, psychiatric symptoms, effects on driving and machinery, and cardiovascular events as warnings and precautions [4]. Wikipedia lists headache, nausea and reduced appetite as common, with anxiety, insomnia and dizziness in 5 to 10 percent of users, and says sympathomimetic effects can raise heart rate and blood pressure [15].

The label notes that intrauterine growth restriction and spontaneous abortion have been reported with modafinil and armodafinil, and that adequate controlled studies in pregnant women are lacking [4]. Users on looksmax.org describe headache, appetite loss and joint aches, and one user described anxiety and sweating with armodafinil that he did not experience with modafinil [8][18].

Modafinil was developed in France in the 1970s by the neurophysiologist Michel Jouvet and Lafon Laboratories as the primary metabolite of adrafinil [15]. It was approved in France in 1994 as Modiodal and in the US in 1998 as Provigil for narcolepsy; the FDA added shift work sleep disorder and obstructive sleep apnea in 2003 [15]. The UK approved it in December 2002 [15].

Cephalon acquired the US rights in 2001 and introduced armodafinil in 2007; Teva acquired Cephalon in 2011, and generic modafinil became available in the US in 2012 after patent litigation [15]. In 2008 Cephalon pleaded guilty to a federal charge over promoting off-label uses of Provigil and two other drugs, paying 425 million dollars in fines and settlements [15]. The FDA required additional label warnings in 2007 after reports of serious skin reactions, and denied a 2008 pediatric ADHD application over skin-reaction concerns [15].

Modafinil is a Schedule IV prescription drug in the US, prescription-only in the UK without being controlled under the Misuse of Drugs Act, and prescription-only but not controlled in Canada; Russia listed it as Schedule II in 2012, and Japan and China restrict it as a psychotropic [15]. The World Anti-Doping Agency added it to its in-competition banned list on 3 August 2004, and athletes in track and field, cycling, basketball and rowing have tested positive [15]. Community threads discuss obtaining it without a prescription; this wiki does not document sourcing.

Press coverage has portrayed it as a favoured drug in finance and as a 'smart drug'; Hacker News threads reflect headlines such as modafinil being Wall Street's new drug of choice (2013) and a paper describing it as enhancing cognition and deemed safe by health experts (2017) [16][17]. Researchers writing in 2020 cautioned that efficacy as an enhancer was not firmly established [21].

timeline.event: Developed in France by Michel Jouvet and Lafon Laboratories as the main metabolite of adrafinil [15].
US FDA approves Provigil for narcolepsy [15].
Orexin knockout mice show a narcolepsy-like phenotype, shaping wake-promoting drug research [11].
FDA adds shift work sleep disorder and obstructive sleep apnea indications [15].
WADA adds modafinil to its in-competition banned list (3 August) [15].
Armodafinil introduced; FDA requires extra label warnings on serious skin reactions [15].
Cephalon pleads guilty over off-label promotion and pays 425 million dollars; Neuropsychopharmacology review of cognitive effects [2][15].
JAMA imaging study shows modafinil raises dopamine and occupies the dopamine transporter in men [3].
Generic modafinil becomes available in the US [15].
Battleday and Brem systematic review of effects in healthy, non-sleep-deprived adults [20].
American Medical Association policy discourages cognitive-enhancer prescribing to healthy people [19].
Meta-analyses of 47 studies report small overall cognitive improvement from modafinil in healthy adults [21].

lore.intro: On looksmax.org modafinil appears in threads about studying, productivity and 'lifemaxxing', often compared with Adderall; T Nation threads treat it as a brain-function booster [8][9][28][31].

claims.claim: Modafinil makes users more alert, productive and focused without the jitters of caffeine.
claims.believers: A medical student described studying for 14 hours without brain fog or jitters, and another poster reported being faster at tasks [8][18].
claims.experts: The label confirms wake-promoting effects in sleep-disorder patients [4]; a 2020 meta-analysis found a small improvement in healthy adults and a 2021 pilot trial found no significant effect on its test battery [21][22].

claims.believers: A reply in a thread says flatly that it is not addictive [18].
claims.experts: Its mechanism involves the dopamine transporter [3] and its label includes psychiatric warnings [4]; registered trials have tested it in cocaine and methamphetamine dependence [13][33].

claims.claim: Modafinil raises charisma and social ability, helping looks and dating.
claims.believers: One poster credited it with making him more charismatic and awake, and with easier social interactions [18].
claims.experts: No published studies have examined modafinil for social attractiveness or appearance.

claims.believers: One thread's author said prescribed Adderall did nothing for him while modafinil was far better [9].
claims.experts: Head-to-head data come from sleep disorders, such as a 2024 trial against amphetamine-dextroamphetamine in hypersomnia, where the drugs are used for different conditions [25][4].

claims.claim: Modafinil suppresses appetite, which helps stay lean.
claims.believers: Users report eating very little on it, and one noted it complicated a lean bulk [8].
claims.experts: Reduced appetite is listed among common effects in Wikipedia's summary [15]; no trial has examined it as a body-composition tool.

claims.claim: Modafinil causes side effects such as headaches and joint aches.
claims.believers: Users report throbbing headache, no appetite and aching joints after use [8].
claims.experts: The label lists serious rash, hypersensitivity, psychiatric symptoms and cardiovascular events [4].

claims.claim: Adrafinil is an alternative route to the same effect.
claims.believers: A T Nation poster described adrafinil as a precursor that the body converts to modafinil [32].
claims.experts: Wikipedia identifies modafinil as the main metabolite of adrafinil [15].

claims.claim: Modafinil is a safe smart drug.
claims.believers: Headlines shared on Hacker News described it as deemed safe by health experts [17].
claims.experts: The AMA discouraged prescribing enhancers to healthy people in 2016, and researchers in 2020 said efficacy was not established [19][21]; the label lists serious warnings [4].
